rules.title: SF Rent Ordinance just cause eviction (§ 37.9(a))
rules.requirement: A landlord of a unit covered by the Rent Ordinance may evict only for one of 17 listed just causes, and the just cause must be the dominant motive. Expiration of a lease or a change in ownership is not just cause; removing housing services such as parking or storage also needs just cause.
rules.key_value: 17 enumerated just causes; dominant motive required
rules.quoted_span: In order to evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have a "just cause" reason that is the dominant motive for pursuing the eviction
rules.coverage_conditions: Units covered by the Rent Ordinance; also covers some tenancies exempt from the rent increase limits (post-June 13, 1979 CO units, Costa-Hawkins-eligible tenancies, some government-regulated tenancies).
rules.penalty: Unlawful eviction or attempted eviction may bring substantial civil and/or criminal liability.
rules.interaction: Applies even to tenancies exempt from the Ordinance's rent increase limitations.

unverifiable_exemptions: tenancies in units regulated by other government agencies may be exempt
owner-occupancy and other exemptions under the Rent Ordinance

rules.title: SF Rent Ordinance annual allowable rent increase
rules.requirement: For rent-controlled units, landlords may raise rent by no more than 1.6% for March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027. Multiply base rent by .016 to get the maximum dollar increase.
rules.quoted_span: For rent-controlled units, the annual allowable increase amount effective March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 1.6%
rules.effective_date_note: Start of the current allowable-increase period announced January 14, 2026 (rate adjusts each March 1); the ordinance's original effective date is not given in the documents.
rules.coverage_conditions: Rent-controlled units; rent limits do not cover units that first obtained a Certificate of Occupancy after June 13, 1979.

unverifiable_exemptions: Costa-Hawkins exemptions (single-family homes, condos) and government-regulated tenancies cannot be verified from parcel data

rules.review_note: Cutoff date taken from the just-cause overview (D079) describing units exempt from the increase limits.

rules.title: SF Rent Ordinance ban on algorithmic rent-setting devices
rules.requirement: Landlords and vendors may not sell or use algorithmic devices (software using nonpublic competitor rental data) to recommend rents or manage occupancy for residential units. Tenants or the City Attorney can sue; tenants may seek damages, injunctions and civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation, with each unit-month potentially a separate violation.
rules.key_value: ban on algorithmic devices using nonpublic competitor data; up to $1,000 per violation
rules.quoted_span: The law prohibits the sale or use of such algorithmic devices and allows a tenant or the City Attorney to bring a civil action if they believe an entity is in violation of the law
rules.effective_date_note: Per SF.gov (official): went into effect October 14, 2024; law-firm alert says only 'October 2024'.
rules.penalty: Damages, injunctive relief, civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation (per unit-month), per law-firm alert

rules.title: SF Rent Ordinance relocation payments for no-fault evictions (§ 37.9C)
rules.requirement: For owner/relative move-in, demolition or permanent removal, temporary capital improvement, or substantial rehabilitation evictions, the landlord must pay each tenant relocation up to a per-unit maximum, plus an extra amount for each elderly, disabled or minor-child household. Amount depends on the date the eviction notice is served.
rules.key_value: Notices served 3/1/2026–2/28/2027: $8,245 per tenant, max $24,733 per unit, plus $5,497 per elderly/disabled tenant or household with minor child
rules.quoted_span: Relocation Payments for Evictions based on Owner/Relative Move-in OR Demolition/Permanent Removal of Unit from Housing Use OR Temporary Capital Improvement Work* OR Substantial Rehabilitation
rules.effective_date_note: Start of the rate period in effect as of 2026-10-01; rates adjust each March 1. Archive shows schedule from 2006.
rules.exemptions: Temporary capital improvement evictions of less than 20 days are governed by Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.9, not § 37.9C.

unverifiable_exemptions: Rent Ordinance exemptions (e.g., government-owned or certain subsidized housing) cannot be verified from parcel data

rules.title: SF Rent Ordinance Ellis Act relocation payments (§ 37.9A)
rules.requirement: Tenants evicted under the Ellis Act must receive a higher relocation payment per tenant, up to a per-unit maximum, plus an extra amount for each elderly (62+) or disabled tenant. Amount depends on the date the notice is served.
rules.key_value: Notices served 3/1/2026–2/28/2027: $11,110.05 per tenant, max $33,330.13 per unit, plus $7,443.90 per elderly/disabled tenant
rules.quoted_span: Relocation payments for tenants evicted under the Ellis Act
rules.effective_date_note: Start of the rate period in effect as of 2026-10-01; rates adjust each March 1.
rules.review_note: Section number 37.9A appears only in a link label in D083 ('Multilingual Relocation Payments 37.9A').

rules.title: SF security deposit interest rate
rules.requirement: Landlords must pay interest on tenant security deposits at 4.2% for March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027.
rules.citation: S.F. Rent Board security deposit interest rate (Rent Ordinance)
rules.quoted_span:
Security Deposit Interest:
4.2% for March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027
rules.effective_date_note: Start of the rate period; rate adjusts each March 1.
rules.review_note: The document does not cite the code section requiring deposit interest; none is asserted.

rules.title: SF Fair Chance Ordinance (affordable housing)
rules.requirement: San Francisco's Fair Chance Ordinance protects residents with arrest or conviction history in affordable housing decisions.
rules.key_value: protects applicants with arrest or conviction history in affordable housing
rules.quoted_span: San Francisco's Fair Chance Ordinance protects residents with arrest or conviction history in affordable housing decisions.

requires_unknown_facts: unit is in an affordable housing project

rules.review_note: Code section not stated on the HRC page; cited by name.
